symptom: A later Director repair fixed the current Rust failures but reintroduced previously resolved named tests; subsequent rounds oscillated and exhausted the bounded repair loop.
root_cause: Two coupled platform defects existed. First, Factory detected a rejected verifier candidate but settled only TaskRuntime and left its bytes on disk. Second, the initial rollback guard re-derived its scope across the roles public boundary and snapshotted the broad owner task path src/lib.rs instead of Factory's explicit causal repair authority src/patience.rs. The guard then reported restored while the actual candidate remained on disk, and Factory reset diagnostics to the pre-round baseline, splitting report truth from physical verifier truth.
required_fix: Snapshot the exact Factory-authorized repair_target_files before mutation through an explicit public service parameter; after real verifier revalidation, CAS-restore rejected or regressive candidates and persist rollback evidence. Never re-derive rollback scope from mutable context/task rows. Do not expand write scope or restart PM/CE.
required_tests: A candidate that reintroduces a regression guard without verified net progress restores the pre-candidate UTF-8 file content.
An accepted verifier-progress candidate discards its snapshot and remains on disk.
Rollback fails closed when the post-effect hash drifted before restore.
Rollback never touches paths outside the Director-authorized candidate scope.
When the owner task target is src/lib.rs but Factory repair_target_files is src/patience.rs, only src/patience.rs is snapshotted and restored.
A rejected equal-count swap restores physical bytes before the next verifier baseline and preserves candidate diagnostics only as rejection feedback.

implementation_evidence.live_revalidation: same-run QA-only retry proved each rejected candidate restored src/patience.rs; Factory report and independent cargo test both ended at tests/edges.rs:15/17

prohibited_actions: restart PM or Chief Engineer for an ordinary Director repair failure
treat prompt presence as proof of candidate acceptance
